newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power steady amid ample supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power steady amid ample supply.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the Southeastern Electric Reliability Reliability Council (SERC)ended Tuesday steady against Monday's levels amid ample power supply in the region, industry sources said.
"There's a major surplus (of capacity) in the area because of the load," said a SERC trader. "The load's been so off,"
Peak temperatures throughout the Southeast were mostly in the 70s and 80s Fahrenheit today, and were predicted to remain at or fall below that level next week.

Last Friday's shutdown of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) 1,148 megawatt (MW) Sequoyah 2 nuclear unit in Soddy-Daisy, Tenn., did little to reduce the ample generation picture in the region, traders said.

Sequoyah 2 was shut to stop excessive leakage on a seal on a reactor coolant pump. The unit was expected to be shut two weeks, according to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission's daily status report on Tuesday.
Next-day electricity for firm, peak delivery into the northern part of TVA was again assessed at $14.00-$15.00 a megawatt hour.
Down at the Georgia-Florida border, firm, peak electricity for Wednesday was still valued at $22.50-$23.50.
TVA reportedly left next-day offers of peak, non-firm power unchanged from Friday at $19.00-$19.50.
